description: Verify that DUT replies to an ARP Request whose target_hw is an arbitrary non-zero, non-broadcast value — receiver must use target_ip, not target_hw, to decide whether to reply (RFC 826 §2.4)
approach:
[Objective]
Close the loop on ARP_16/17 by injecting an arbitrary non-trivial target_hw. Reply must still happen because the only criterion is target_ip == DUT iface IP.

[Scenario — chronological]
1. Tester → DUT: ARP Request injected
   • opcode      = 1
   • target_hw   = some arbitrary value (not zero, not broadcast)
   • target_ip   = DUT IP
   • sender_*    = HOST-1-IP / MAC-ADDR1

2. Observation (3 s window):
   • DUT → Tester: ARP Reply (opcode 2, sender_mac=DUT, target_ip=HOST-1-IP)

[Pass condition]
DUT emits an ARP Reply within the observation window.

[Fail condition]
Fail_no_reply — DUT did not reply. Likely cause is over-strict reception that filters by target_hw matching DUT MAC, contrary to RFC 826 §2.4.

verdicts.Pass: DUT replied — arbitrary target_hw tolerated as required
verdicts.Fail_no_reply: DUT did not reply — over-strict target_hw filter (RFC 826 §2.4 violation)
